properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/07/2025 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Elkland Township, Sullivan county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/07/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8240136
Permit API: 113-20482
Unconventional: Yes
County: Sullivan
Municipality: Elkland Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/07/2025
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of produced fluid. The release occurred at the frac tanks near the wells just to the northwest of the wells. At the time of inspection, the quantity of released produced fluid was unknown but was reported to be at least 1 barrel. I met onsite with Mike Deming, Expand. There were two sets of containment, each approximately 70' long by 55' wide. The staining appeared to be concentrated near the front-center of the tanks and between the two sets of containment for about half the length of the tanks. There were some holes identified in the offload area of the secondary containment shown in Photo 3. Soil conductivity was checked using a Groline soil conductivity meter. The damp areas/fluid were greater than 4.00 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm) which is the upper limit of the conductivity meter. Expand indicated that the conductivity of a few puddles in these areas was around 21 mS/cm, having used a YSI meter. There were no other puddles on the pad surface or seeps found between the pad and the infiltration basins. The soil conductivity below the pad and in the basins ranged between 0.05 mS/cm and 0.68 mS/cm.The set of tanks in the foreground of Photo 1 are going to be cleaned and removed in order to pull the containment. Some of the tanks in the background of Photo 1 will also be removed and the containment lifted as much as possible to facilitate a full assessment and remediation of the impacted area. The remediation is tentatively scheduled to begin 7/9/25.Per a discussion with Mike Deming, the site will be remediated under Act 2 requirements. The result of this inspection is Violations noted for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a). There are also outstanding violations for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a) due to a release documented in inspection 3981577 from 5/20/25 and inspection 3982600 from 5/22/25. The release detailed in those inspections is also undergoing Act 2 remediation. The violations may be closed after the completion of Act 2 remediation.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8230575
Permit API: 123-48946
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Pleasant Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/17/2025
Comments: Bull Run Resources contacted WQSS Brian Ayers to inform him of a release that occurred overnight on April 16, 2025 their Peterson P9 well, located in Pleasant Twp Warren County. I arrived on site and spoke with Sam Harvey from Bull Run. Sam informed me that the cause of the release was a high pressure stuffing box on the well head failed for an unknown reason. The emergency low pressure switch on the well head also did not function as designed. Production fluid was released from the well head and traveled downslope following a series of road ditches and culvert crossings. The release does not appear to have progressed past a power line located just north of the well. Several underflow dams have been constructed in the ditch lines and are working effectively at this time. Absorbent pads are being used at the siphon dams to collect any production fluid accumulating behind them. The quantity of the release is estimated between one half to one barrel. Bull Run was having roll off dumpsters delivered while I was onsite. Impacted soil will be removed and disposed of at an approved facility.Upon completion of the remediation, confirmatory samples are expected to be collected and their results provided to the Department. Documentation verifying the disposal of the impacted soil is also expected to be provided to the Department.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to DANNIC ENERGY CORP in Huston Township, Clearfield County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/07/2026 to DANNIC ENERGY CORP in Huston Township, Clearfield county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DANNIC ENERGY CORP
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/07/2026
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8274489
Permit API: 033-25738
Unconventional: No
County: Clearfield
Municipality: Huston Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/07/2026
Comments: Routine site inspection on May 7, 2026 with DEP representatives Sue Herzing, Justin Galioto, and John Salinkas. The well appears active and capable of producing. Approximately 30 BBL of brine fluids were measured in the 100 BBL brine tank. Flakey paint and corrosion was observed on the production equipment and axillary pipes. The Department recommends monitoring the equipment and repainting or replacing the equipment if needed. A 5x Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. No combustible or methane gases were detected. Please note, during the inspection and area of exposed soil (~2'x4') was observed to the right of the brine tank (photos 3-4). I screened the exposed soils and elevated readings were observed with 2.01 mS/cm being the highest reading (photos 5-9). A soil sample was collected 3442-976 and sent to the Departments Lab in Harrisburg and will be tested for SAC 530 plus bromide, lithium, and strontium. While onsite, we contacted Dannic Energy well tender Rob Yohe via phone. Rob was in the area and met us onsite. Rob explained that when he arrived onsite Monday, May 4, 2026, he found that the dump line coming off the well head had corroded off where it connects to top portion of the brine tank and was lying on the ground. The other section remained attached to the well head. He explained that he removed the pipe. He noted, that the well was shut in when he found the dump line lying on the ground. Rob stated that only residual fluids were in the dump line. I explained to Rob, that elevated soils were discovered and that these impacted soils will need to be removed. I contacted Dan Sinclair and left him a voice message regarding my findings. Rob hand excavated impacted soils based off visual impacts to the soil (photos 11-12). I recommended that he cover the excavated area with plastic. The Department recommends screenings the excavated area. Screenings need to be <1.00 mS/cm before being backfilled.Violations have been cited for the brine release. The Department recommends cleaning up spill in accordance with "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites or Access Roads (800-5000-001).

Inspection Date: 4/21/2026
Comments: On 4/21/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 52 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. When I arrived at the active north pad, I met with Seneca's Adam Pierce who described current operations as follows: Evolution Well Services has been on site since 2/13/2026, performing stimulation operations on eight recently drilled gas wells. The crew was currently alternating between the 70HU, 204HU, 203HU, and 72HU. The crew has completed conducting stimulation stages on the other four wells. Adam expects stimulation activities on the eight wells to be completed by 6/8/2026.In addition to 28 frac tanks that were stationed on the west side of the pad during previous operations, four freshwater frac tanks, four pump down frac tanks, two gas buster frac tanks and five working frac tanks have been staged on the pad. These tanks are staged in secondary containment.Five wells have been completed at the site and were staged for production. Two produced water tanks and five GPUs that are connected to the completed wells are stationed in secondary containment.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. During the inspection, I screened liquid in a 3' x 1.5' x 5" deep puddle, above the center outfall on the north side of the pad, the result being 9.40 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-242 from the puddle.I screened liquid flowing into the southeast corner of the sediment basin from the rock lined outfall from the pad, the result being 10.30 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-243 from the flowing liquid.I screened liquid in the sediment pond next to the east overflow, the result being 3.04 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-244 from the pond.I screened liquid flowing north from the sediment basin, past the last compost filter sock and past the LOD, the result being 3.33 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-245 from the flowing liquid.The original south pad and access road for the Taft 851 1V well have been returned to original grade with vegetation becoming effective. Separate construction projects are underway, installing water and gas pipelines on the south side of the pad.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1545 hours.

Violation ID: 989371

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 3/21/2023
Comments: On 3/21/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Stoorza well site. This inspection was to assess the condition of the storage piles of excavated contaminated material that was transported from the Chesapeake Grippo well site. It was 50 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. There are three piles of excavated material on the pad surfaces. The south pile is estimated at 60' x 100' x 12' tall. The northeast pile is estimated at 40' x 50' x 12' tall. The northwest pile is estimated at 40' x 50' x 15' tall. The three piles are stationed in secondary containment with a plastic liner protected by a fabric liner. The piles are covered with a plastic liner. I did witness a separation to the plastic cover on the south pile. I also witnessed a separation to the berm wall on the north side of the south pile. There was visible damage to the plastic secondary containment liner on the south side of the northeast pile.In close proximity to the excavation piles, I field tested water puddles on the unprotected pad surface fir conductivity with an Oakton PCTS 50 with the following results: A 12' x 6' water puddle on the unprotected pad surface at the north edge of the southeast excavated material pile field tested at 3.18 mS conductance. A 3' x 2' water puddle on the south side of the northwest pile of excavated material field tested at 5.44 mS conductance. A 3' x 12' water puddle that was approximately a half inch deep on the unprotected pad surface on the south side of the northwest excavated material pile field tested at over 20 mS conductance. A 20' x 15' water puddle along the east side of the northeast pile of excavated material field tested at 4.36 mS conductance.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. The site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by three retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designedThere were two wells staged for production. Both wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The GPUs and production tank had secondary containment.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the pad surface is a violation of CSL 402(b). The failure to contain regulated substances within secondary containment is a violation of 78a.64a(b). The DEP recommends the following:1. Due to the elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface. 2. Assess the condition of the excavated piles secondary containments and repair as necessary.3. Recommend daily monitoring of the site until waste is removed.I left the site at 1650 hours.

A 3' x 12' water puddle that was approximately a half inch deep on the unprotected pad surface on the south side of the northwest excavated material pile field tested at over 20 mS conductance. A 20' x 15' water puddle along the east side of the northeast pile of excavated material field tested at 4.36 mS conductance.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. The site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by three retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designedThere were two wells staged for production. Both wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The GPUs and production tank had secondary containment.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the pad surface is a violation of CSL 402(b). The failure to contain regulated substances within secondary containment is a violation of 78a.64a(b). The DEP recommends the following:1. Due to the elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface. 2. Assess the condition of the excavated piles secondary containments and repair as necessary.3. Recommend daily monitoring of the site until waste is removed.I left the site at 1650 hours.

Inspection Date: 7/07/2025
Comments: On July 8 2025, the Department conducted an inspection of the McMichael Well Pad in regards to a spill that was reported to the Department on July 8 2025 at 9:12am . Present during the inspection was Brandon Carson.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Act 9 sign was posted at the access road entrance in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), and the Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan (PPC), both of which contained all required components, were located within the on-site mailbox. The access road appeared to be stabilized with gravel.Upon arrival at the well site remediation efforts appeared to be nearing completion as the remaining excavated material was being placed into the roll off dumpster. Mr. Carson identified the location of the spill. According to Mr. Carson, ,the spill (which occurred on 7/8/2025 at 7:15am) was reportedly caused by a 2" hydraulic line failing on the snubbing unit during work on the 14H well. This resulted in a release of hydraulic fluid to secondary containment as well as the graveled well pad. Mr. Carson estimated 50 gallons of hydraulic fluid was released in total with roughly 35 gallons releasing to secondary containment and roughly 15 gallons releasing to the graveled well pad. A vacuum truck was utilized to recover standing hydraulic oil. At the time of the inspection, Specialized Professional Services Inc. (SPSI) was onsite remediating the impacted area.Mr. Carson stated the contaminated gravel was excavated near the initial location of the spill approximately 6-8 inches in depth. Additional gravel was excavated in the area the hydraulic fluid flowed to at a depth of approximately 1 inch. The excavated material was placed into one roll-off box located on site. The Department was unable to obtain conductivity readings in the location of the spill as the gravel pad was too heavily compacted. However, the spill appeared to be visually remediated in accordance with the current regulations.Upon inspection of the rest of the pad, the Department observed 7 other well heads which appeared to be properly tagged and surrounded by protective barriers. The production tanks and GPUs onsite appeared to be within secondary containment with no visible fluid leaks or spills.Based on observations from this inspection and information provided by the operator, it appears that the spill has been remediated in accordance with current regulations. Violations are being issued as immediately corrected for the release of hydraulic fluid outside of secondary containment.

On 10/12/2023, violations of 91.34(A), 78.66(b), 78.57(a), 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.53, 102.11(a)1, and 102.22(a) were issued as outstanding for the observed elevated conductivity and the access road condition. No elevated conductivity observed (Photos 1-6). The operator had placed the impacted soils within buckets that were dated (Photos 7, 8).Some soils were removed from the berm adjacent to tank 5. No elevated conductivity observed (Photos 9, 10).Regarding the area behind tank 5, it appeared as though the area I initially discovered to have elevated readings, and the operator was not able to replicate my readings, displayed adequate readings on 10/16/23, most likely due to dilution from rain (Photos 11, 12). There was one reading of 3.29 m/S, however this area was small, approximately a 4 inch by 4 inch section (Photo 13). The operator is going to remove some soils from this area, which was marked with a brick (Photo 14). Due to the size of this area, no violation is being noted.The operator explained that the cause of the impacted berm was due to fluids reaching the ground during tank clean out (Photos 15, 16). It is highly recommended to place containment/grate to collect any residual fluids and prevent them from reaching the ground and berm during tank clean out.The access road appeared to remain in poor condition (Photos 17, 18). Inspection Date: 12/02/2020
Comments: The operator called the Department to report a spill at the Burning Well PV-81 well site on December 2nd at 9:20 am. The Complaint ID for this spill is #353829.A tree near the well fell due to heavy snow and wind overnight onto the lead line of the well, causing a union to fail. The well is pumped with an electric powered pumpjack that is on a timer. This well begins to pump at 8:00 am. At 8:30 am, the well pumper came by and found the well leaking. He immediately shut the well in and informed the operator of the spill. The tree was cut off the line and the flow of oil was stopped. Dave Hill plus two well pumpers from PVE were on site when I arrived, as were three representatives of Howard Drilling, who had been called to help clean the oil up. They were using a portable vacuum tank to collect any loose oil they could find. The oil appears to be caught in the snow in an area approximately 15-20 feet circular down gradient from the spot of the leak. No oil flowed outside this area, as heavy snow acted to slow and prevent seepage. It appears as though 10-20 gallons of crude oil was spilled from the compromised line. The operator has cleared the top of the tree from this area to begin cleanup. Snow and debris have been cleared at the edge of the contaminated area. The operator has placed a continuous pile of absorbent peat in this cleared area around the spill as a berm. They intend to rake and shovel the oily snow and debris to the center of the area, then load it into two or more plastic totes that will be used as temporary storage. The entire area will then be covered again with peat for the time being. When conditions allow, they intend to dig up any soil that is contaminated and haul it to the landfill, along with the oil covered sticks from the site. Continued inspection will be performed on this site as cleanup progresses. See attached sheet for violations.

Inspection Date: 4/06/2022
Comments: The DEP conducted a routine inspection of Repsol's DCNR 587 02-003 well site located in Ward Township, Tioga County on 4/6/2022 at 1030 hours. The weather was 49 degrees with an overcast and very light rain. Rain fell onsite overnight and is forecasted to rain more later in the day. DEP Environemntal Trainee, Brooke Millisock, assisted me during the inspection. We met with Billy Watts (Repsol) to discuss work that Repsol plans to have done on the access road. During the inspection, a large amount of mud was observed on the access road due to recent rainfall mixing with sediment present on the road. Repsol recently installed 18-inch silt sock along the roadside to prevent further sedimentation off the side of the access road. Today, sediment-laden water was observed discharging into Fellows Creek along the northern shore, below the access road bridge (photos #1, 11 & 12). Sediment-laden water was also observed to be dripping from the bridge into Fellows Creek as truck traffic crossed the bridge. The bridge top is constructed with metal plating and sediment-laden water is seeping through the cracks. Rocks utilized in the construction and stabilization of the bridge (photo #6) were also observed to be covered in a layer of the sediment. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/13/2024 to RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC in Fawn Township, Allegheny county. OGA3218.2(A) - CONTAINMENT FOR UNCONVENTIONAL WELLS - SITES - Failure to design and construct unconventional well site to prevent spills to the ground surface and off well site.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/13/2024
Violation Code: OGA3218.2(A) - CONTAINMENT FOR UNCONVENTIONAL WELLS - SITES - Failure to design and construct unconventional well site to prevent spills to the ground surface and off well site.
Violation ID: 8187543
Permit API: 003-22657
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Fawn Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/13/2024
Comments: On May 13, 2024 the Department conducted an incident inspection in regards to a spill that occurred at the Sun Mine Well Site (ESCGP-3 issued on 9/11/2023 and expires on 9/10/2028) on May 10, 2024. According to Derek Zofchak of Range Resources, the spill occurred at 12 PM when drill cuttings and soap slurry fluid entered the flare stack eco tank (which normally separates fluids from gas), the float on the pump within the eco tank malfunctioned and as a result, fluid (approximately 30 gallons of drill cuttings and soap slurry) that normally would not get carried over to the flare stack ended up spewing out of the flare stack as a fine mist onto the graveled well pad and well pad fill slope. At the time of the inspection, Range Resources notified the Department that the spill had been remediated. Two roll off dumpsters were on site filled with waste material, the well pad appeared to be scraped on the left hand side of the flare stack, and new seed and mulch was seen on the the fill slope and berm directly in front of and to the left-hand side of the flare stack. Soil conductivity readings were taken to determine if any areas were still contaminated, a background was done on the far back side of the well site perimeter upslope (0.03 mS) then readings were taken outside of the approximate release area to the far left of the flare stack on the pad (0.0085 mS and 0.016 mS), then moving forward into the approximate release area (0.0146 mS), another was taken fairly close to the flare stack on the left-hand side in a wet looking spot in the gravel (0.327 mS), directly next to the flare stack in a wet-looking section of gravel (0.293 mS). Then a reading was taken from the right side of the flare stack where Range claims was not impacted and therefore was not scrapped (0.088 mS). A reading was taken directly behind the flare stack right at the base of the berm before the fill slope (0.138 mS), in the berm directly behind the flare stack (0.081 mS), outside of the area that Range replaced on the fill slope where they say was not impacted (0.130 mS), and lastly three were taken from the area of the fill slope that was replaced (0.100 mS, 0.131 mS and 0.209 mS). Based on the soil conductivity readings, it appears that all contaminated material that was present on the fill slope, berm and the well pad to the left/in front of the flare stack has been removed. Range stated that the flare stack eco pump was taken apart for examination and nothing was found to be wrong with it. According to Range this was just a random malfunction and they do not anticipate that it will occur again. The Department recommends Range place the flare stack inside secondary containment in case this were to occur again.Based on todays inspection the Department concludes this release has been immediately corrected in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1).

Report Details

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8244601
Permit API: 129-28648
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Fairfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/07/2025
Comments: On August 7, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Burnett Oil Co Inc's Stickle Ross Mountain Unit 1H well (129-28648) located in Fairfield Township, Westmoreland County following IR 4011505, where the Department observed several areas of the graveled well pad to have an oily substance on it, specifically in areas relating to the reported re-plugging of the 129-28648 well. Accompanying during today's inspection is Monona Operator/Land Owner Tom Stickle and Plants and Goodwin's Representative Jim Watson.Burnett Oil representative Walter Glasgow stated in an email to the Department (documented in IR 4029448), that clean up began on 7/28/25 and was completed on 7/31/25, once the Department conducts an inspection of the site to determine if all contaminated material was removed, Burnett will replace the removed rock from the graveled well site. Once Waste Management disposes of the contaminated material, Burnett Oil will provide the Department with a quantity of the release. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed an Act 9 sign at the access road entrance to not be in compliance and inside the on-site mailbox was an outdated Emergency Response Plan (ERP). Violations associated with the Act 9 Sign and the ERP are addressed under a separate inspection for 129-28411. An access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel and the perimeters of the well site were observed to be exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative cover with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed.At the time of this inspection, the 1H: 129-28648 well appeared to be plugged and all plugging equipment appeared to be removed from the well site. A new monument and vent pipe which was reportedly approved by the Department was observed to be installed. The monument was observed to have the plugged well's permit number and replug date posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this plugged well.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the graveled well pad to be scraped in the areas that were previously observed to have an oily substance during IR 4013514. At the time of this inspection, the Department did not observe an oily or shiny brown substance anywhere on the graveled well pad. Mr. Watson stated that all contaminated material was placed in the roll off dumpster observed on site, that new gravel will be laid in the release areas and the contaminated material will be properly disposed of following this inspection. The Department requested a waste manifest for the disposed contaminated material be provided to the Department upon its receipt to verify whether the release was less than 42 gallons, and therefore remediated applicably under 78a.66(c)(1). If the quantity of the release is over 42 gallons, the Department recommends the Operator follow the Act 2 guidelines for remediation as set by 78a.66(c)(2).Based on today's inspection, violations issued for an oily substance on the graveled well pad shall remain outstanding at this time pending the receipt of a waste manifest and a quantity of the release.

Comments: On 6/18/2026, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill (CTS-398645) at the PA Game Commission well pad in Blaine Township, Washington County. The spill reportedly occurred on 6/17/2026 at 8:05 PM, when approximately 20 gallons of produced water/condensate released from a water hauler truck. The Department received the spill report from the operator on the same day at 9:59 PM. The operator reported that the spill was in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1).An Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) for this site was terminated on 8/06/2018The following was observed during the inspection:The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment appear to be sound at the time of inspection. A rolloff box is on site that reportedly contains the impacted material (photo 11). The old GPU/Vertical Separator Units are not equipped with secondary containment (photo 12). However, the associated gas wells were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. The new GPU/Vertical Separator Units are equipped with interconnected secondary containment drip pans (photo 13). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the Department for use on 6/21/2022. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.

Wellhead is located in soybean Agriculture field planted/harvested ~380' SSE of surface/ground production equipment (photo #1). At the wellhead surface casing valve is open, lower right side production tubular valve cracked open to port with valve to port closed, production tubular left side valve is closed, and the production tubular plumbed on left side of head to sales/surface equipment with open valve; annulus is exposed and vented to the atmosphere with plumbed tubular sticking out of ground and open valve union (photos #3 and #4). The shared, multiple, two well (085-24005 and 085-23892) surface/ground production facility, two 50 bbl poly tanks, and two 100 bbl steel tanks all contained by a shallow earthen dike (photo #5). The Department is requesting Operator add contact address information to the permanent well posting signage affixed at the surface production facility. The Operator has not submitted 2021 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well. No MIA submitted by the Operator for 2021, 2020, and 2019. The last MIA value officially submitted was back in 2018 stating 55 psig. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Operating Wells - Mechanical Integrity reporting 78.88(e). The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2021 of 172 Mcf recorded over 365 days. This is an active, producing well.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/08/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/08/2026
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8277568
Permit API: 123-47192
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/08/2026
Comments: Evidence of stressed and dead vegetation in the vicinity of the Akins lease tank battery was visible from Rounds Hill Road. Brian Ayers (WQSS-DEP) and I (Mat Haemer WQS-DEP) were present for this inspection. This inspection was conducted to document findings of an apparent release of production fluids from the Akins tank battery, as well as a separate release from a brine tank previously removed from the nearby Loomis lease's tank battery. Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners previously indicated that he had checked and found the integrity of the Loomis lease brine tank to be sufficient for future use. Kyle indicated that the tank was empty and would be unused until repurposed.The PVC drain line within the secondary containment area of the Akins tank battery was found to be improperly placed. The PVC line straddles the cutout hole in the surface of the brine tank in such a manner that fluids draining through the line would be able to flow over the surface of the brine tank and pool within the secondary containment area. Soil within secondary containment immediately below the PVC line was found to have specific conductance in excess of 17,000 micro Siemens per centimeter. Evidence of pooling was visible in the containment area via crude oil staining and stressed vegetation. This indicates that fluid once filled the secondary containment, but apparently was able to migrate downward and/or outward through the secondary containment diking. Stressed and dead vegetation downslope and immediately outside the secondary containment dike further indicates the likelihood that the integrity of the secondary containment is inadequate. Understory vegetation was killed in an area approximately 30 feet wide by 200 feet long. Soils in the killzone were found to have elevated specific conductivity in excess of 2,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.The brine tank staged on location was found to have evidence of stressed and dead vegetation beginning from a point immediately beneath the drain valve and continuing downslope beyond the tank in an area approximately 10 feet wide by 200 feet in length. Specific conductivity in soils below the drain valve measured in excess of 8,000 micro Siemens per centimeter. Soils in the killzone downslope of the brine tank were found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 2,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.Because the volume of this release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold, the use of either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required.It is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners provide the Department with brine disposal receipts for the Akins lease. The Akins Lease Akins 1 OG Well was found to have an illegible ID tag.

Inspection Date: 1/13/2026
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Blackhill Energy's Kline B well pad located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 1/13/2026 at 0815 hours. The weather was 28 degrees F with mostly clear skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by the operator. Complaints Tracking System (CTS) ID #394552 is tied to the release in CTS.On 1/12/2026, Blackhill Energy reported to the DEP that approximately 1 barrel (42 gallons) of produced fluid was discovered to have been released to the pad surface at ~0730 hours. The release occurred after condensed fluids within the low pressure pipeline were pressurized and were able to escape through a 2" connected pipe (photo #1). Blackhill reported the release within 2 hours of discovery and began remediation as soon as possible. During remediation on 1/12/2026, scraping of the impacted material and recovery of fluids was mainly superficial due to the pad materials being frozen. Throughout the remediation process, temperatures rose, thawing some of the pad material and requiring a couple locations of deeper excavation. Impacted materials were placed within 2 lined residual waste containers onsite (photo #5). During my inspection, pad materials within the impacted areas were field measured for electrical conductivity and returned readings ranging from 0.1 to 2.2mS/cm. Fluids located closest to the impacted area were field measured for electrical conductivity below 1.0mS/cm. The DEP recommends continuing screening and recovery of any impacted materials and collecting characterization samples to confirm that cleanup is complete. Based on the reported release of ~1 barrel of produced fluids to the pad surface, outside of secondary containment, violations of the following are cited against API #015-22301 at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)35 P.S. 6018.30135 P.S 691.402(b)I departed the site at 0945 hours.

Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#373559). As part of the investigation 3 slam bar holes were placed into the ground approximately 1-2 feet from the well head to identify if any methane was migrating from the well-bore. All valves were open and the well is currently equipped for production. 2 check valves were in place on the production lines and were oriented correctly. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/27/2021
Violation Code: 78A57(A)___ - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator discharged brine and other fluids on or into the ground or into the waters of this Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 924677
Permit API: 125-27390
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Smith Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/27/2021
Comments: On July 27, 2021, I conducted an inspection of the Harmon Creek Well A 11323 Well Site in Smith Township, Washington County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release of fluid reported by the Operator to the Department on 7/26/2021 at 16:00. The Operator reported that approximately 1.5 barrels of production water and condensate was released to the well pad due to a sight glass o-ring failure on the Gas Production Unit (GPU). At the time of inspection, the Operator was in the process of the removing the GPUs from the area impacted by the release. I observed a petroleum odor and dark staining under the middle GPU and excavated channels on either side of the middle GPU. The impacted area appeared to be approximately 30’ x 10’ in size. The staining was visible approximately 12" in depth. I spoke with Range Resources representative Nick Reda. Mr. Reda indicated that the released material was proximity 51% production water and 49% condensate oil and that the Range intends to utilize Act 2 for cleanup. No waterways were impacted by the release and no apparent migration of the material was observed. Two roll off waste disposal boxes were on site to collect the impacted material for disposal. The Operator is in compliance with the current Department spill policy for reporting the release. Violations area being issued for the release.

Comments: On 11/19/2024, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the PALUSO F45MK OG Well in Fallowfield Township, Washington County. I was accompanied by PA DEP ET Olivia Holley.The following was observed during inspection:-A well tag was observed on the well head (Photo 1).-The well and operator's information was displayed and visible at the well site as required by OGA 3211(g) (Photo 2).-Corrosion was observed on the well head and pump jack. I observed over range fluid leaking from a valve on the well head. Elevated conductivity of 12.09 mS/cm was observed on the ground below the valve (Photo 3-8).-Some corrosion was observed on the production tank and production equipment (Photos 9 and 10). I observed additional equipment and pipes being stored on site (Photo 11-13).-Disturbed area that may be related to a spill. Attempted remediation appeared to have been conducted in front of well site/well head (no vegetation). The department wasnt notified of a spill. Elevated conductivity readings were found throughout the 6 x 6 ft non-vegetated area. Lowest reading was 2.94 mS/cm and highest was 6.94 mS/cm (Photo 14-25).Field Scout Conductivity probe was calibrated before inspection was conducted on 11/19/2024. The operator was contacted on 11/19/2024 and notified of elevated conductivity readings and violations being issued.Violations are being issued for: 78.57(a), 78.54, SWMA 301, and 91.34(a)
